title: Trying to comprehend the mother - sadness thing
content:
This is somewhat about our relationship but ultimately about it as a reflection of having become parents of young children, thus why I’m posting it here.

Husband / father here. I feel very immersed in what my wife is feeling and what she’s been saying. A lot of it I see here (things like: I feel touched out, life is just so hard, I struggle to get in touch with my sexuality, I don’t know what I want, the mental load is just so hard). I think I was too eager to “fix” things before, whirl around like Tasmanian Devil making her life easier so that the world wouldn’t get her down. I am now realizing her feelings are not mine to fix. Not truly, anyway. And with that realization I’m more in touch with what she’s saying.

I still don’t fully understand it though. Part of my realization is I don’t have to fully understand to say “I believe you.” I’d like to understand though. Why the sadness? Our lives are hard. Two really challenging (but amazing) boys ages 6 and 3. Older one is high functioning autistic / ADHD and we suspect younger is ADHD, struggling with some executive function stuff, so they’re a handful, but amazing. Full-time jobs. Friends, family, major city with smaller space and high cost of living. It’s hard, it makes me sort of chronically exhausted and burnt out, and under slept. But not sad. I sense so much sadness on this subreddit. I know a lot is due to clueless incompetent ungrateful husbands. I am disappointed in my fellow husbands. I am one of the good ones—I could explain why or you could take my word for it. I suppose you could read the above and conclude I am clueless and don’t share an equal burden. That isn’t the case, but I’m not going to argue that here. Well actually I will a bit further on.

I’m just wondering what it is. If the husband is good, what is it then? Identity shift? More difficult to become “mom” than “dad”? Harder expectations from society? No one congratulates me for anything I do as a husband or father, but maybe I don’t feel the same societal pressure to be perfect.

Husbands/Dads (good ones at least) are tired too. I know my friends are. I don’t think anyone is sad though. I feel like this has become a CORE part of her identity. “Everything is so hard” is her catch phrase. I don’t want to disagree with her experience but my god I feel like she embraces it to a fault. It has become a choice.

Just to preemptively retort any suggestions/questions, I take care of my children. I do the majority of the cooking, grocery shopping, buying them clothes (about a 50-50 split that one). She was traveling for work a lot, I racked up weeks of single parenting experience (cumulatively). I’m the more domestically inclined one in general. I handle my share of administrative tasks (although she does more here, and I strive to improve that balance). I woo my wife. She is as hot as she’s ever been. I am accepting of where she is, and that can mean giving her space. Lots of space. I strive to let her initiate sex. Our sex life is good. Our sex has always been extremely good. And I take care of myself and it isn’t a breeze. My alarm is set for 4:45am to workout almost daily, so it doesn’t interfere with the rest of our lives. I’m in the best shape of my life, and I handle the mornings with the kids in full, breakfast, lunch making, etc, letting her sleep in u til 7:30-7:45 or so. I love the opportunity to handle things so she can go have some fun.

I told her recently I am a little worried about her. And I confessed “I feel like you used to chase me. Now only I chase you. I don’t remember the last time I felt chased.” I just want her to be happy. But I can’t fix it. I can do things to help. Identify where the mental load is greatest and relieve it. Secure more hired help, which I do. But we aren’t at war, we are living privileged lives, we’re very lucky in many many ways. I came from a briefly happy family that became a broken home wrought with alcoholism (mom and dad). I am so grateful to have a family of four under one roof again. Why is the burden of motherhood flipping this sadness switch? I can help, but I don’t see our lives getting easier anytime soon. I can’t change that.

title: Is there any piece of wisdom you can share with me that will help me get my life together?
content:
I was a lazy, messy, disorganized person before the baby, so it’s my habits I want to blame. I never prioritized self-care or cleaning — it didn’t bother me before. But now, it’s not what I want anymore.  
I’m tired of living in a mess and washing my hair only when it’s absolutely necessary.

I have a 14-month-old toddler and a full-time working husband (he works from the office, away 5 days a week for 10–12 hours). We don’t have money for a nanny, and I don’t have the guts to do daycare.

I spend all day with my little one. I don’t mind it, but I want to do more around the house or go out more often.

Right now, the apartment is a mess, food is all over the place, laundry never makes it into the closet. We just grab clean clothes from the basket or the couch (when the basket’s too full). I keep throwing away veggies and leftovers because I either forget about them or just can’t find the time to cook.

Our day looks like: whatever the baby chooses to do, that’s what we’re doing together. He can’t play alone for long, and if he’s not in the mood, he wants me to hold him or sit with him.

We go out to toddler classes once a day, but he’s not a fan of the stroller and doesn’t walk long distances. So we can’t really go far from the house, 10 to 20 minutes is my max, because I don’t want to carry him in my arms for longer than that.

I work out twice a week during his nap, and naps are the only me-time I get during the day. I also have 1–2 hours before I go to sleep. I don’t wake up before the baby, and I’m not sure I’m ready to start doing that.

title: Selling kids' stuff I paid for and keeping the money?
content:
Edit: I feel like almost no one gets the idea here. 

I am NOT taking my kids stuff away without their permission. I am also not selling their toys and clothes for massive amounts of money and using it on myself.  They are fine with what goes out of the house, they just feel *I* should sell it and *they* should get the money. 

And examples of the stuff I'm referring to are tables and chairs I bought for the playroom (basement), a giant train table (bought used) that I don't think is worth selling. It's 20 years old and missing some cosmetic pieces. Someone would love to have it, but I would feel ridiculous being paid for it. 

And I do feel like this is a life lesson for them: we chose to be more present parents which means we don't have the money that everyone else has. We are frugal with our spending and roll any money we make from what we sell into the next thing we/you need. And most importantly, because I have boys, the value of invisible labor. Nothing comes or goes for free. It either costs money, time, physical and or emotional labor or all of the above. 

**OP**
We tend to be somewhat "minimalist", I guess you would say, with our money. It's always been more important that we're able to spend time with our kids than have high paying jobs. (That's a topic for another post.) Over the years I've worked mostly part-time jobs but I'm always the one to buy the extras for my kids. Things that my husband doesn't think are important. And I'm always particular about them having nice clothes and shoes, so I do a lot of bargain shopping, thrifting, etc. 

Our house is super cluttered, so I've been going through a lot of stuff and sorting out what I can donate and what can be sold. My opinion is I paid for all of these things. And chances are I'll just flip the money over and buy the next set of nice shoes, or Adidas jacket, or whatever that next thing is. I feel like that is clearly my money. When it comes to things like toys the kids (11 and 14) feel like they should get that money. They also get irritated over things that I don't feel are valuable enough to sell. They tell me I'm, "always giving stuff away" when it could be sold. Listen, I have done my time on marketplace, ebay, poshmark, etc, I know what has value and what doesn't. I know what's worth the effort and what isn't. I also see things like nice coats, boots, gloves, swimwear, might be something a family needs or would love to have but can't afford and I would rather see those things get donated. In short, I'm the adult! 

But sometimes I do feel a little guilty. Like I'm taking something away from them but they're not getting anything in return. But trust me, they have enough of everything. I'm just trying to figure out if I'm wrong here. If I sell their clothes are they entitled to that money? I don't know, I'm really on the fence. 

And let's be clear! We are not talking about a lot of money. I could probably sell every "extra" thing in this house and walk away with about $300. 😂

title: What is your beach vacation "schedule" like with young kids/toddlers?
content:
We've gone on a few beach vacations with our kids (3 and 4), and I feel like our "schedule" is a bit much (though our kids enjoy it and they're used to it by now). But I wonder what other people do.

We take a few long weekend beach vacations a year since we live fairly close to a coast and we stay in a reasonably priced hotel with a pool. The hotel room isn't large, so we don't want to spend a ton of time in the room. We maximize our time outside since we belong to a pool at home. Our days typically look like this:

Morning - eat breakfast, play a little, head to the beach until lunch. The beach is next to a boardwalk so we'll leave the beach here and there for a snack. One of the days we'll mix it up and do a little boardwalk bike ride/pool instead of the beach.

Early Afternoon - Lunch in our room, then youngest naps while the oldest plays for "quiet time" or takes a nap if she's tired.

Late Afternoon/Evening - so this is where I get tripped up. We don't want to spend the afternoon in the hotel room, so we typically head to the beach after the youngest finishes their nap, we'll get there \~330/4ish, give or take (sometimes they're into playing/coloring and don't want to leave right away). Then, we typically hang out on the beach until dinner (we eat dinner out each night at the boardwalk, it's very casual. I HATE cooking dinner on vacation - how does one find the time to do this if you're out and about having fun?). By then, it's usually too late to go all the way back to the room to clean up and then head back our for dinner, so we rinse them at the rinse station and change them into dry clothes in boardwalk bathrooms/changing area, and go straight to a casual boardwalk dinner from there. After dinner, we'll stroll around and do some games/rides/snacks until bedtime. Then we're back at the hotel. Bedtime is often later than it is at home, but they don't seem to notice or mind. One of the days we'll usually do afternoon boardwalk rides/games instead of the beach.

I feel like that's not what most people do - but the logistics of doing it differently hurt my brain. If we packed up and headed all the way back to the hotel to clean up before dinner, it would be too late for dinner and everyone would be hangry. It can be difficult to get them to leave the hotel room once we're there. But if we leave the beach earlier, they wouldn't get much beach time in the afternoon. Seem like a waste after packing up, suiting up and slathering on sunscreen for round 2.

Curious how other people with young kids schedule their beach vacations?

title: How many loads of laundry are you doing a day? [UPDATE]
content:
A couple of weeks ago I posted on here asking for advice on how to cut my laundry down, I was typically doing 2-3 loads a day and was constantly behind. 

I was flooded with a ton of great advice! It helped me reflect on my laundry habits, re-evaluate and start to tackle my laundry in a smarter way. And, it worked! I have successfully cut down my laundry to 1 load every 1-2 days!! Crazy! I’ve completely caught up on laundry, and even managed to do a free load for my son’s daycare, and it didn’t put me behind! 

I thought I’d share the tips I received and how I did it! 

Turns out - I was washing clothes entirely too often. Every time my boys got wet I’d throw the clothes in the washing - now I let the clothes dry and they re-wear them (unless they’re smelly) 
At the end of the day whatever outfit they were wearing I’d automatically grab the clothes and put them in the washing, thanks to your advice I realised this was silly - I now check to see if it actually needs a wash, some things can be re-worn again! 

If my clothes were sitting on the floor I’d just put them in the washing. I’m now being more cautious to put them on the dresser until I can get to them, and I let them air out instead of rewashing just because they’re not fresh. I used to change my pants regularly if they got dirty from the kids, now I wear them all day and am less over the top about it. A couple marks isn’t a biggie. 

The BEST advice I received that has truly been a game changer - someone mentioned they give their laundry an extra spin before chucking in the dryer. ABSOLUTE GAME CHANGER! 

Every load of clothes gets an extra spin, and towels get 2 or 3 extra spins. My drying time has cut down by 2/3rds. Waiting for the dryer to finish was what was truly slowing the process down. And guess what? Now that I’m giving the clothes an extra spin, I can load more into my washing machine. It’s like a 2 for one bonus. 

I’m still mostly washing my towels after single uses, it’s hard to get them to dry right now. But it’s okay, my towels aren’t piling up, the washing isn’t piling up, everything is manageable. Even on the day I had to wash 2 sets of bedsheets. And throw blankets. And couch covers. 

I want to thank you all for your great advice, laundry is no longer daunting or stressful! Absolute legends!

title: My 20-year-old daughter lives at home rent-free… and has opinions.
content:
Im a mom of 4 — 20F, 16M, and 11-year-old twins (M & F). But today, I need to vent about my oldest.

So my 20-year-old daughter still lives at home. She graduated high school, didn’t go the college route, and has had a few jobs here and there, but nothing consistent. I’ve never pressured her to move out because hey, times are tough, and I get that. Rent is expensive. Life is hard. That’s not the issue.

Here’s the issue: she doesn’t want to pay rent. Not even a little contribution. No help with groceries. No real household responsibilities unless I ask five times. But she somehow still manages to have new clothes and nails always done.

When I brought up rent — even something small, like $150/month just to teach responsibility — she got defensive. Said I was being “money hungry” and that “family shouldn’t charge family.”

Meanwhile, I’m covering her living, her WiFi, electricity, groceries, everything — all while still raising three other kids.

I’m not trying to kick her out. I just want her to start transitioning into adulthood, and that includes contributing to the household she lives in. Or at least offering to help. I’d be happy with initiative!

I don’t want to create tension, but I’m starting to feel taken advantage of. Has anyone dealt with this?

title: Son (5) and daughter (3) play inappropriately(but innocently)?
content:
I’m not sure how to put this because it truly doesn’t feel sexual in nature at all but at the same time, it doesn’t matter.
My son was diagnosed with level 1 autism, he’s a really loving kid but struggles with boundaries. He can get very physically in your face and up close more than the average person is comfortable with and it’s something we’re working on teaching.
Both siblings adore each other and overall get along better than most siblings I think. The problem is they play inappropriately sometimes. They’ll be play fighting and laughing and I look over and she’s got her legs spread and he’s just ramming his head into her private area and she’s laughing. They’re both clothed, they aren’t being sneaky or acting like what they’re doing is bad but I’m struggling to get them to understand how they can’t be SO close. They think licking each other is silly too and will sometimes put their faces together and try to touch tongues. Again, not a making out motion or anything but still obviously not something that they need to be doing.
I don’t know how to drill it in their heads that that kind of behaviour isn’t ok and knowing they’re still coming from a place of innocence I don’t want to make them feel particularly shameful.
I tell them not to touch tongues or  be near each others private’s but that’s obviously not coming across serious enough.  It’s hard when they’re both laughing too, if one was upset it would be obvious that it’s “wrong” but when they’re both laughing and thinking it’s silly it makes it more difficult to explain to them how it’s still wrong.
I love that they are really close siblings and best friends but obviously boundaries need to be made clearer and I don’t know how to do that.

title: Need Parenting Advice: Taking in My Husband’s Troubled Teenage Daughter
content:
I (34f) could really use some advice from other parents right now.

My husband (33M) has a daughter who’s turning 13 this month. She’s lived with her mom her whole life, but it’s been very unstable—she’s been to 11 different schools, moved constantly between cities and states, and lived with different boyfriends. Her mom has struggled with alcohol addiction and poor choices, and although my husband has always tried to stay involved, their relationship has been rocky. She even blocked him for several months recently, and we had no way of contacting her, or no way of understanding why or what was going on. 

Last week, her mom called to say she had run away. We happened to be visiting family in their city for the holiday, so we immediately helped look for her. After three days, she was found at a trap house, where high she had been getting high on meth. We learned this wasn’t the first time. Her mom seemed somewhat unbothered afterward and just told my husband to hang out with her for the next few days.

We’ve since learned a lot more from the mom’s aunt and uncle, who they have been staying with, since we've been here. Her mom is barely around—she’s back to heavy drinking and using drugs with a new boyfriend. The daughter has also been drinking, vaping, smoking weed regularly, and has used coke and meth multiple times. She’s been suspended for fighting and just switched schools again. She spends hours (sometimes 7+ straight) scrolling TikTok. She wears extremely revealing clothing, tiny booty shorts and low cut tops on the regular basis around town.

Her great aunt and uncle begged us to take her in, saying she’s being neglected and is in danger. Her mom is moving in with the new boyfriend this weekend, and again seems distracted. So here we are. We’re bringing her to live with us.

My husband and I live in a small 2-bedroom townhouse with our 18-month-old son in a larger city. Space is tight, and we’re already stretched thin, but we want to do everything we can to help her feel safe, supported, and cared for. She’s never lived with us before—only short visits here and there.

I’m looking for advice on how to set her up for success. We know she needs structure, clear rules, and positive outlets—but we also want her to feel safe and not like she’s being punished. How do we balance firm boundaries with compassion and care? What can we do to help this poor girl get back on track?

title: Natural consequences for bedtime delays/not listening
content:
Just need some ideas for bedtime silliness. Our routine is pretty consistent (no screens, quiet play, snack at 7:30, brush teeth, get dressed, book, head scratches, goodnight by 8:30) but way too long and some nights we aren't out of the room until after 9:00 (he sleeps on his own).

Big part of the problem is daycare let's him nap, and even though I've begged them to cap it, they always forget and he sleeps for up to 2 hours.

But still, he's a delay expert. He'll add steps like putting on lotion, removing and refolding clothes, "cleaning his room", and asking for a million things. Then he will alternate between wiggling away from the head scratches/yell at me for stopping. Sometimes his behaviour escalated to the point where we would normally do a time out (hitting/throwing things).

I'll try a natural consequence of "no head scratches because you took too long" and then he throws a screaming tantrum and runs out of the room. I've tried the natural consequence of, "you're not listening to me, so dad (the non-preferred bedtime person) will have to help". Dad's more old-school and will take away his music box or a teddy bear (not my style, but effective).

It's not most nights, but it's annoying and I don't feel like We have a solid plan.

title: 16 year old and chores
content:
My 16 y/o daughter was looking for a job this summer but due to her schedule with drivers Ed and cross country pre season practice (she also does winter track and spring) it was difficult.  I told her I would pay her $50 a week to do about 30 minutes of light housework (make her bed, pick up her laundry off the floor and bring it to the laundry room, empty out the dishwasher, keep her bathroom clean and put the laundry in the dryer).  Nothing crazy.  In fact I think it’s kind of the bare minimum.  She agreed but complained the whole time (I am working on my MSw and working part time so I wasn’t home to hear the complaining).  Yesterday I noticed her shorts were a little snug so I offered to get her some clothes. She picked out some shorts and tops and it was about $135 total.  I said ok.  Today I asked her when she was going to start her chores and she said, later.  It’s 11:30 and we said she had to have things finished by 11am (she gets up around 9).  She got mad at me and went to her room and slammed the door.  I feel like I got played.  I bought her the clothes and I am asking very little.  She gets good grades, she’s a hard worker, but when it comes to keeping her room clean or doing chores she can be really difficult sometimes and other times she just does what needs to be done.  Not sure were we go from here now.  Just needed to vent.
I should note- I buy my kids plenty of clothes-  in fact too many as I have been told.  It was about being appreciated.  Which I feel like I wasn’t.

title: My Newborn is Not Here for Your Amusement
content:
I love my in-laws. I just need a good rant about them every once in a while. We have brunch together most Sundays kind of family. They are very kind and welcoming but also a lot sometimes. They're loud, high anxiety, and come from a culture that believes the older generation is always right. Baby's great grandma is leaving the country for 2.5 months, so we went to Sunday brunch even though I was not really feeling it. My toddler needs to get out of the house daily anyway. 

I put my 10 day old in the baby carrier because I was feeling protective. I didn't really want to pass her around and there were more people than usual to see great grandma before her trip. The realities still complained the entire time the was in the carrier that she was sleeping. People were all up in my business trying to get a look at baby. One family member kissed the top of her head, so I covered it with some cloth to keep it from happening again. The next time they went for her cheek right next to her nose. I took her out right before feeding her, but not when she was fussy yet so great grandma could hold her and my MIL tried to steal her immediately. They have a saying in their culture for good luck/protection and they said it so often it felt more like a jinx from over protection (I know this one is rediculous but I just pushed a watermelon out of me 10 days ago). Then great grandma told me I should be resting for 40 days. The same great grandma who complained that we had not brought baby over yet 3 days ago. 

My baby is her own person. I am happy to help facilitate a relationship with her family members because that is what is best for her. But I don't want to get her sick this young, or have her passed around like a toy, or feel like she is everyone's amusement for the afternoon. She spent most of her life so far inside of me, yes she wants me more than she wants you. She does not know you yet.

title: Nothing is ever enough
content:
Hi all,

I'm the stepmother to a beautiful and intelligent 8 year old girl. I have the summer off, so I've been spending most of my days with her. 

Ever since I've known her (4yo), she's always been one to want something in each store we go to (which I feel like is typical kid behavior.) I have never given into that. I always make it clear what we are there for and remind her whenever she starts insisting and my husband does the same. It has always been fine and she usually just goes "okay" and moves on. I thought that as she got older, this would lessen, especially since we are consistent about this. However, this summer has just begun and I'm finding her attitude about wanting things a little over the top. 

Every time I say no to a request, she will be in a bad mood for most of the day. 
Here are some recent examples:
- I got a new phone because mine was starting to malfunction. She was upset when I opened it because she didn't get one too. 

-We went to a furniture store for a lamp and she was upset that I didn't buy her a new bed because  "her's is old"- we bought it 2 years ago. 

- She asks me daily to go buy fast food and most of the time I say no. 

-I made a little basket of things for a friend who just got very sick and she was mad that I didn't make one for her too.

-I got a cake for my sister's birthday, and she wanted her own cake.

Each time, I calmly explain why she can't have or doesn't get something. Mind you, last year, I re-did her whole room with her to make it a cozier and comfy space. She has plenty of clothes, toys, etc.

It's never been THIS bad.

Parents, what do you do about this? How did you correct (?) or change your kids' habits about needed to have more all of the time? Or needing to get something whenever someone else gets stuff. My husband and I are lost. He doesn't have reddit, so I'm the one posting. We're worried that it's just going to keep getting worse.

She spends half the week with her mom but I don't know how things are on that end since it isn't a friendly relationship.

Edit: format and extra information.

title: Our 3 year old is hurting our well-being
content:
My wife and I are struggling. We have 3 kids, 5.5F, 3.5F, and 2F. I like to think that our kids have been raised with a healthy balance of autonomy and limitations. The older two have access to a tablet with restrictions, screen time gets eliminated if we recognize they're being excessively whiny and clingy and needing attention or alternatively if they're being hateful to one another and short-fused. Our basement is a hodge-podge of toys, trampoline, bounce-house, sensory swing, roller coaster ride, bunk bed/fort thing etc. Backyard has a playset, plenty of room to run around. They interact often, but they also fight all the time. Our children can sometimes be helpless, we try to foster a good level of help yourself and we'll help you. The 3.5 year old sometimes will ask for a cheese stick and I'll say go ahead and get one and she does just fine. Sometimes she'll get it for herself without even asking. Sometimes she'll ask me for one and i open it and all hell breaks loose cause she wanted to open it (she can't and asks for help all the time). We've gotten into a habit of asking if she wants to do it or she would like our help on almost everything. We're tolerant of accidents, but we are not tolerant of purposeful messes. She will leave the wrappers all over the floors and refuse to clean them about 50% of the time. I pre-address and say we need to make sure when we're done we clean our areas, and again, 50% of the time this works, 50% of the time she straight up refuses. No consequence hold weight and if i try to help her and/or use her hands to clean it up we enter potential scream territory.

We'll use today as an example - last night they were promised pool time today, we needed to eat breakfast, run an errand, and then pool around 1030. Kids and us interacted great, we had a fantastic morning. We get ready to leave and home girl absolutely refuses to get dressed. We pick out clothes, she doesn't like that, we offer for her to get clothes, she wants us to do it. We ask for her to help us pick something out, she doesn't want to do that either. We give her choices and she wants long-sleeve (it's 100 with heat index). We have the long-sleeves packed away and we tell her as much, she doesn't care. We are firm that we have her clothes available, she can choose, we can choose, and we can choose together but if she is not dressed we can't go. This is about a 15 minute scream meltdown before we ultimately start walking out the door and she agrees to wear what we've packed. This is very minimal in the grand scheme of things, but this behavior, not this situation, is an every day occurrence. We've tried to help her calm down, she refuses. We've tried to do some funny and silly methods of breath control (smell the flowers, blow out the candle, balloon breaths, animal breaths) and we've attempted counting, distraction, ignoring and she just refuses to do any of it, even while calm she will not take deep breaths for us to recall upon later. These are not meltdowns where she's quite, she stomps, screams, screeches and ear piercing screech, and follows us around - she will not sit in a calm place. We have lost our patience many a times and we have yelled and yes i know, we need to eliminate that but the frequency of these events makes it so difficult to hold our cool, especially when it's nap or bed time. Fast-forward, we got to the pool, we eat a good lunch, nap time (she doesn't like to nap and will fight us again, scream bloody murder if we even so much as hint that she needs to sleep) so we try rest and if she doesn't she doesn't). She didn't want to nap - i had to do some work painting our chairs and tables and she wanted to help. The paint was getting a second coat and when they helped me last time i had to redo it all cause it was smudgy and with the material the chairs were it was very streaky, so  i recommended our splash pad. The 3 of them are playing and all is well. Mom is napping during this, when she wakes up mom goes to the store to get groceries and other things for the home. We asks her what she wants for dinner, noodles, we make her noodles. Our other kid had tacos, we made enough for her as the 3.5 year old doesn't eat tacos so think nothing of it. Her plate gets made and she wants tacos. We didn't make enough (and again, she doesn't eat it) so we try to be understanding, tell her we don't have enough tacos and that we've made her noodles like she requested. Nope, she wants x, y, and z. I try to stand firm on this type of stuff but my wife is very much the kid needs to eat (she's a 0%iler so anything she eats is better than nothing). She gets x,y, z, and eats 5 bites before declaring she's done. Again, don't really care but slightly annoyed cause this again, is a common (not as common, but frequent enough) event.

Final and most regular straw - she is *tired*. 6:30am wake up, 2 hours at the pool, no nap, an hour+ in the splash pad and she's running on E. They get waters for bed, normally it's a non-issue, sometimes both of my big kids will lose their shit if they get the wrong cup. We always try to choose a cup we know there's not issues with but that's not always the case. She went ballistic over a cup and she was going ballistic before hand - i think i zoned out during this one cause i can't remember what for - but she just continued on and on about a different cup and we said take it or leave it. She continued to scream, mom warned her that the screaming needed to stop (she was preventing oldest from sleeping and youngest was now stirring from it in a separate room). She continued to scream about the cup, mom left the bedroom to maintain herself as we were both getting irritated as bedtime is our #1 most stressful time, especially when the wife and i are both home as they both fight over who gets her. Anyways, screaming intensifies, i can't get her calm, breathing doesn't work, oldest is now upset because she can't sleep, she makes a beeline towards the door and i stop her because we're at wits end. I tell her she needs to lay down in her bed and she continues to screech for another 10 minutes. I just try to "sleep" by the door so she can't leave. Eventually, i send my 5 year old to our bed and i leave the 3.5 year old in her room to scream alone. I don't know how to fix this and the screams are so frequent that i literally can feel all my muscles and feelings clench that second it starts. We can't take it anymore and we don't know what to do. I am 100% no more tablets, my wife is a little less so on that front. TV is mostly just background but occasionally we'll watch a movie. We're not the most actively playful parents but we do interact with them often.

Any advice or things to try would be amazing...



EDIT: Thank you everyone for your responses, I've felt that my expectations were too high to begin with and this post really highlighted that I am at fault here. My kids seems so emotionally intelligent in other areas that it is hard to sometimes remember they're as little as they are. I have struggled with my own inability to handle overstimulating situations calmly and i think it's reflected poorly on them. I've picked up some books and will spend some time working to improve my own self-regulation and expectations for a better relationship with the girls.

title: My 12 year old daughter has told me she wants to be a boy
content:
Hi everyone,

I’ve been carrying a lot on my heart lately and could really use some thoughtful, kind support as we navigate this new chapter with our 12-year-old daughter.

Up until about 8 months ago, she was very into makeup and traditionally feminine clothing. But after becoming close with a new friend, she’s started expressing herself differently—she now dresses more masculine, no longer wears makeup, and seems to be exploring a new identity.

Her friend is transgender, which we didn’t initially know. I learned more after seeing some texts and eventually talking to the friend’s parent. That’s when I realized the name my daughter had shared with me wasn’t actually their legal name, but rather the name and pronouns (he/him) her friend chooses to go by. I want to be clear: I have no problem with her being friends with someone who is trans, and I truly like her friend.

Since their friendship began, I’ve noticed a lot of changes in my daughter. I recently found a breast binder that her friend gave her…As well as a journal they share where she appears to be using a different name for herself. When I gently asked her if she wanted to be a boy, she said yes. I told her I love her unconditionally and reminded her that she’s still very young and growing. Let’s give it time to see if that’s how she feels in a couple years.

I’ve continued to support her in ways I feel comfortable with: buying her clothes that she feels good in, listening, and doing my best to keep the lines of communication open. But it’s also been hard. We live in an area where acceptance isn’t widespread, and some of our family members have reacted negatively—suggesting we transfer her schools or stop her from seeing this friend, which doesn’t sit right with me as they have many similar interests. But I still wonder if this friend has been heavily influencing these recent changes in her.

I’m trying to hold space for her journey while also feeling uncertain and scared—scared of how the world will treat her if this is who she truly is. It breaks my heart to think of her being rejected or hurt, especially by people we love.

I don’t have all the answers. My husband is struggling with it, too—he loves her deeply, but I think he’s still processing. We just want to do what’s best for her, while also navigating our own fears and confusion. Is this a phase? We just don’t know.

I’m open to kind, respectful thoughts from others who’ve gone through something similar or who can offer perspective. Please know this comes from a place of deep love for our daughter. We’re just trying to figure out how to support her the best way we can.

Thank you for reading.

title: Figured out why my toddler was impossible to dress
content:
(tl;dr he was hangry)

My almost-2 toddler was impossible to dress for a few months. I read every piece of advice I could, but I felt like I was living on another planet.

Give him choices? Obviously. Not too many choices? Sure, but he will say no to everything no matter how many. Let him wear his favorites? What favorites?? Try different textures? You wouldn't believe how much money I spent on weird niche clothes trying to find something he was happy with. You get the idea. So many exhausting, heartbreaking, late to work mornings.

You know what else was going on? He's terrible at eating. Like occasionally gets scary underweight. Like if we lived in a place where food therapy was accessible, he would be on it, and if it gets much worse we'll be making a long commute. He was falling behind again, so even though he was already on 1 daily bottle of pediasure to get baseline nutrition, I doubled that (pediatrician endorsed).

Suddenly getting dressed in the morning got SO easy. A lot of other things did too. He got more relaxed and happy about just about everything.

It wasn't that he was upset about getting dressed exactly. It was that he was hungry, or had low iron, something like that, and dressing was one of many things that didn't feel good.

(At least that's what it looks like.)

My takeaway is, if I'm having a hard time with a child and the usual advice doesn't even make sense, check on sleep or food or other fundamentals as the real root problems. Just sharing the advice I wish I had found months ago.

title: Wicked, Barbie, Legally Blonde - a rant
content:
These movies all present supposedly critical takes on the concept that being blonde, perfect and beautiful is the ideal.  I guess the idea is to show that perfection and looks arent everything.  

But if that's the intent, the message is going over the head of my girls (mainly the 11 year old).  She has become obsessed with these movies and have come to idealize the blonde perfection of the characters in them.  She wants to dress like those characters, maybe dye their hair, etc. (My girls are mixed -- part-east-Asian btw).

I (father) never decided to let the kids watch these movies, they saw them with friends, at people's houses etc.  In my experience, many endorse these films because of the critical msgs, and are happy to have their kids watch them, but what my girls take from them is : its great to be blond, beautiful and wear really expensive clothes.

Maybe that's out there anyhow but the movies sure didn't help.   

And yes parents need to send own messages as well and talk about things..  I'm not denying that parents have to parent -- but our cultural environment has its effect, and there is alot of parental endorsement of these films (esp Barbie & Wicked).  As I said  I (father) never decided that the girls would watch them - they saw them at friends houses on the airplane etc.

I should say that also appreciate the other movies (eg Moana) that project other norms of ideal girlism.

edit:  I take the point that these movies aren't meant for an 11-year old, but she and her friends have all seen them anyhow (she watched Barbie on the airplane, for eg, Wicked in the theatre).  Policing the viewing if is pretty much a losing proposition when other parents are all bought into them

title: Confront or Let Go
content:
Hello,

Never posted before but I've run into a situation I'm needing perspective on.

I'm a 46 year old single mom of a two teen sons, the youngest who I'll call H, just turned 17.

I had previously shared custody with my ex-husband, until 2 years ago H decided he wanted to live with me full time. My ex-husband has a very toxic lifestyle, causing H to respond with aggression and defensiveness. It took about a year for H to decompress from the experience and become more 'apart' of my household.

Around that time, H met a girl his age, I'll call her M.

M is a sweet and quiet, she's a good student and has a plan for her future. Her values don't exactly align with our families but I'm not going to attempt to control H's choices for obvious reasons. This is a learning opportunity for H regardless of my opinions which I've already shared with H.

In the year H and M started dating, M's mother who I'll call S, has bought H melatonin to sleep, a prom tux, multiple pairs of shoes, expensive dinners, and high end clothing. These were not gifts for H's birthday or Christmas, these were just regular provisional purchases.

S bought these things for H without the courtesy of discussing with me, his mother, first. S has my phone number and we've shared a meal before. I don't mind S buying things for H, I feel disrespected because she has stepped into the provider role for H.

As a parent, S is also making it difficult to parent H, who is still a headstrong teenager. If I so no to a purchase be it as a consequence for poor behavior or otherwise, H is very aware S will buy what I won't,

Recently, S asked H to go to out of state with her and M for a horse riding tournament M was apart of. This out of town trip would require two overnight hotel stays.

Two days prior to the trip, H mentioned it to me and asked to go. When I inquired about who was going and where he would stay, H told me he would stay in the hotel room with M & S. I laughed and asked if a male member of H's family would be joining them? H said no, it would just be him, M & S.

My response was no, he wasn't going. During the discussion with H, S started texting me and offering to get H a separate room if it made be feel better, she had plenty of points.  I texted back saying I had already told H no, he wasn't going.

I'm discovering that M & S work together to get H what he wants if I put my foot down with him.

I was disappointed and shocked that S would ask my 17 year old son to go on a trip with her and her 17 year old daughter, without asking me first. Even more so that she took on what, what felt like to me, a teenager role, by asking if H could go after I had already told him no.

Finally, H got his first real job, working with a contractor doing demolition and he needed a good pair of work boots and jeans. 

H went on a shopping trip with M & S, to buy M clothing for her horse trainer internship. While there, S decided to buy H a pair of $120 jeans and an $80 pair of work boots, and again S didn't bother to reach out to me; I had already purchased these items for H.

After dealing with this for many months and not saying anything, I'm seeing a pattern of behavior from S that I don't agree with and believe needs to be confronted but I'd like to hear from others with an unbiased opinions.

Should I have a discussion with S or just let it go?

title: Need some help being a better husband/parent
content:
Hi all,

For context: I live in the UK, have a 6 month old and have been married for 3 years. I'm writing this post because for the past few months in particular (though I'd say, since our child was born), my marriage has been in a bad place, and much of that has been exacerbated by the challenges of parenting. 

It came to a head the other week when my wife and I had a big, blow out argument that we really hadn't had for a long time. It began when I was loading the dishwasher and my wife got angry with me that I wasn't loading it properly, despite her showing me "how" to do it. This escalated to accusations I didn't know how to do laundry efficiently so it'd dry quickly, that i am often forgetful when it comes to remembering to add anti-stain soap on clothes the little one has pooped in etc. It then escalated further as I was then accused of caring more about work than our child (I run my own business and it has been challenging to keep it running while also parenting, even as I've moved most of my operation home), and ultimately, that I care more about myself than my wife or my child.   
  
While the scale of escalation obviously is the result of tensions built up over a longer period of time and not necessarily about just the dishes, it was an insight into just how torn our household has become and the divide between my wife and I. We haven't really had any intimacy in well over a year as she didn't really enjoy any of it while pregnant, and that has now extended to hugs and kisses too where both of us seem to have lost any real desire at all. Our child also struggles to sleep and doesn't like other babysitters etc. so we tend to be fairly round-the-clock parents out of necessity. This obviously means that for my wife, she is feeding regularly, and she often tells me that on the one-two days I might need to go to a client site or to my office (I work in sound engineering and sometimes you do need tech equipment that I can't have at home) she'll go the whole day without going to the toilet, but in a way where it feels like she's blaming me for that. 

I'd like to think I try hard as a parent; I shifted the way that I work to be at home more, I spend the morning hours (5am-9am) playing with our child, reading to them, taking them for walks, tummy time, excercises etc. I make the baby's food, I make lunches and dinners regularly, I try to do as much DIY as I can to make things in the house run smoother. But, it still feels like this isn't enough, that the problem fundamentally is that I get more semblance of my 'old life' than my wife does, and that the arguments and fights mainly occur because of this. 

Whenever I've spoken to her about this, the answer I usually get is that as a male, I will never understand the mental load – that I will never operate in a way where I truly understand the constant state of stress and panic a mother feels – even if i try and write it all down or take up some of it, it doesn't \*really\* matter in the bigger scheme of things. Which leaves me with the question – well, what do I do? It feels as if this dynamic sets me up to fail regardless, and that in spite of doing more parenting than other dads I know, I still feel like im inadequate, failing as a parent and a husband, and as a result, feeling utter resentment constantly. I'm not looking for sympathy or anything, but I am just wondering if   
  
a) there is something I'm missing in terms of what can be done?  
b) Has anyone ever been able to resolve this problem?  
c) Should I shut down the business and just move to being a full time parent? And then when my wife returns to work next year, I can just continue doing the stay-at-home dad thing?  
d) What does my wife actually want from me? (Before being told 'ask her', I have hesitated because once again, questions like this add to the mental load and I don't really want to do that).

Thanks,

title: SAHM looking for small ways to make a little extra income
content:
I’m currently a stay-at-home mom. Before having my baby, I was a clerical sub and a college student.(20) I’d really like to contribute financially, but due to ongoing health issues, I can’t stand for more than 30 minutes at a time without needing to sit for at least 20. That rules out most part-time and entry-level jobs, since they usually require being on your feet constantly.

Even if I could physically manage one, childcare in my area is so expensive that a minimum wage job wouldn’t even cover it. We would actually lose money. My partner covers all necessities, but there isn’t much extra, so I pay for my own "luxuries" like clothes, skincare, hobbies, small things for around the house, ect. He treats us to small date nights every couple of weeks and covers things like getting my nails done once in a while, which I really appreciate. But even those little extras can stretch the budget, so I’m hoping to find a way to contribute a bit myself without adding more financial pressure.

Since the baby was born, I’ve been using my savings for my own expenses, but that obviously won’t last forever. I’m going back to college in the fall, and thankfully my school provides free childcare during classes. That will help, but gas costs are still a concern, especially because my current vehicle isn’t a great fit for our needs.

Last year I bought a lifted truck with only partial back seats. At the time, I was just a college student with no kids yet, so it made sense. I figured I could have a fun car and worry about a family vehicle later. Well, birth control failed due to medical negligence (very long story), so “later” turned out to be now.

Once we installed the car seat, we realized the back seat has no seatbelt buckles. I didn’t know that when I bought it, and I’m not even sure that’s legal. It does have LATCH hooks, so the seat is secure, but it’s definitely not something we can rely on long term. On top of that, the engine has modifications that require premium gas, which makes every fill-up even more expensive.

I want to start saving and feel confident about eventually getting a more family-friendly vehicle. But right now, I’m just trying to find ways to bring in even a couple hundred dollars a month.

So I’m asking other stay-at-home parents (or anyone really): how do you make a little extra income each month without leaving the house or being on your feet all day? I’d love any ideas. Even small, manageable income streams would be a huge help. Thank you in advance.

title: Daughter being bullied
content:
My daughter is 10, short, and scrawny. She is goofy and fun loving and really does try to be everyone’s friend. There is a boy in her grade, more than twice her size, who has been bullying her. It’s been happening for a while, little incidents happening here and there that the school will send a note home about and then do nothing else. Today, they were at lunch and she was sitting across from this boy (not her choice, assigned seating) he told her that he hated her and then threw a slice of cheese at her face. She told him to stop and said he was being mean (all of this was recounted to me by her, two other students who saw the interaction, and a student teacher). He told her that he didn’t care and proceeded to mock her. As they were lining up to leave the lunchroom he continue to mock her, making fun of her, making fun of her father (her dad is the SRO, he called him bald but to be fair he is bald) which really upset my daughter and she began to cry. When she started to walk out of the lunchroom her grabbed and pulled at her pant leg causing her to fall. He walked away calling her a cry baby. When a teacher finally decided to intervene, my daughter was visibly upset and crying. She begged them to call me so they did. I live 3 minutes from the school so I immediately headed up there to talk with her principal and her teacher. I wanted to know why no one intervened beforehand (there excuse was they were allowing time for conflict resolution among peers 🙄), what was being done to prevent this from happening again, and if this boy was facing any disciplinary action. They informed me that they had also called his mother who was on the way and that they planned to make the boy apologize. I told them that I would wait there for his mother and his apology. When she got there, we were sitting in the principal’s office. She came in and when the principal explained what happened, I kid you not, she busted out laughing. I was stunned. She said, “he was just being a goofy boy.” No. No maam. He threw something at my daughter, mocked her, pulled at her clothing, and caused her to fall. This plus weeks worth of “minor incidents” that have been occurring on a daily basis. When the boy came in to apologize he said, “I sowwy” in a babyish mocking tone. I asked him if he could please try again and his mother said, “no he can’t. That’s good enough.” These two go to school together and play on the same little league baseball team together. My daughter, who loves little league, wants to quit because of him and cried, begging me not to send her to school anymore. The teachers and administrators don’t seem to want to take any real action and it’s obvious his mother doesn’t plan to either. I’m honestly at a loss for what to do. There’s only a week left of school but she obviously still has to go and I don’t want her to quit a sport she loves just because this kid has honed in on her. 
Any advice?

title: I am losing my mind and myself. How do some of you parents do it?
content:
I am a mom of 4. It’s a blended family and my SD is 15. Biologically, I have three boys 12, 5, 4. All three are diagnosed adhd. I want to focus on the younger two though. 

I work part-time and go to school for my masters full time (hybrid style). My husband is deployed for a little in Europe somewhere. I am now the only full time parent and I am drowning. We are considered middle class but we are always struggling to keep up with bills and past debt. So that’s an added on stressor. My two youngest boys are absolutely insane. They are not in school yet, and could never afford daycare, so they have been at home for their whole lives. 

My five year old is also autistic, and he is exhausting. He struggles with potty training and I’m always having to clean up fabric, hard surfaces, clothing, bedding, etc every single day. The volume in the house is non stop at the highest possible level. Overstimulated is not even the word I would use for how drained it all makes me feel. Their dad is the hard-ass, military, authoritative one, while I am the forgiving, passive, and loving one. When he is gone, the dynamic is skewed and the kids know it. All. Of. Them. They all take advantage of the weaker parent, and that also bothers me because I feel like I should still be respected even if I am the “softer” parent. I had to leave my house just now and go sit in a Dollar General parking lot because I “had to get detergent”. That was a lie. I just had to get out of the house. I feel like I can’t breathe, and like my body is always tensed up, and my stomach aches and I get so nauseous. This is a daily thing. My mental health is shot. There is no bright light or silver lining because tomorrow is just another day of this horror show. 

I know one day I will look back and miss my babies, but right now I can’t even stand being present. I don’t know what to do to make me feel better and be able to parent the way I need to. does anyone have experience in this, or advice, recommendations, anything? I feel so so defeated and depressed and I don’t know when, or if that’ll ever change.
